items.title: Protest to crackdown: The aftermath of Jantar Mantar
items.summary: In this week’s South Central, hosts Dhanya Rajendran and Pooja Prasanna discuss the aftermath of the Jantar Mantar protests, led by the Cockroach Janta Party. They are joined by senior journalist and editor of The Wire, Seema Chisti, and Peek TV co-founder Vedanta Agarwal. Seema Chisti begins by commenting on the government’s denial of the use of pellet guns and violence on the protestors. “The government keeps denying this, but we must also take note. The CRPF chief was quoted as saying to go for the protests fearlessly. But I am unsure what that means with the government using force nonetheless. The government also seems to unleash a lot of demonstrative brutality on all kinds of protests across the country. This is to show how people who raise dissent will be treated. But this generation is not typical in the sense that they come from all parts of the political spectrum, and that is also confusing and scaring the government,” she says. Vedanta says that now we are seeing an outreach to Gen Z by the government. “We see politicians use Gen Z words in Parliament as well. There seems to be an attempt to turn this into a homogenous, elite movement. This one-size-fits-all outreach to Gen Z is unfortunate. The protests saw people from all cross sections, and that is the truth. This has been a diverse movement. There was also a time when senior journalists said why we should cover protests, but people were still turning up for various protests. Just because mainstream media does not cover it, and numbers were small, we cannot normalise ignoring protests or protestors being ignored. On July 20th, my cameraperson and I were caught in a crossfire. The government had issued orders to the police to clear roads at all costs. Tear gas was fired from both sides of the Sansad Marg, and protestors were running all across to save themselves. Protestors took shelter at a Masjid there, and police were using batons, lathis and gas to clear the roads. We spoke to multiple victims, and they said that the police pinned a group of women to a wall and fired rubber bullets, causing permanent damage to their ears for many,” he recalls. Pooja notes that the orders may have been to clear roads, but the intention of the police seems to be something more sinister, considering the use of such brute force. “I think, in their desire to distort what India is, and how generations move and revolt, the BJP has forgotten that people have agency. History is replete with incidents where the chil

items.title: क्या थार बन गई है 'मर्दानगी' का सिंबल? लड़कियों ने क्या कहा
items.summary: थार सिर्फ एक गाड़ी नहीं रह गई है. भारत के कई शहरों और कस्बों में यह एक खास तरह के वर्चस्व का प्रतीक बनती जा रही है. सोशल मीडिया पर थार के वीडियो देखें तो अक्सर एक पैटर्न दिखाई देता है. तेज रफ्तार, खतरनाक स्टंट, ट्रैफिक नियमों की अनदेखी और इन सबके साथ एक आक्रामक रवैया भी थार और उसके मालिकों की छवि से जुड़ा है. बड़ी गाड़ी, ऊंची सीट और दमदार इंजन कुछ लोगों के लिए सुविधा का नहीं, बल्कि सड़क पर वर्चस्व दिखाने का माध्यम बन जाते हैं. कई बार यह व्यवहार उस पुरुषवादी सोच से भी जुड़ जाता है जिसमें आक्रामकता को मर्दानगी का प्रतीक माना जाता है. मानो थार महज एक गाड़ी नहीं, बल्कि ‘मर्द होने’ का एक स्टेटमेंट हो. लेकिन असल सवाल यह है कि महिलाएं थार के बारे में क्या सोचती हैं? क्या वो थार चलाने वालों को जज करती हैं? क्या बड़ी गाड़ी सचमुच किसी की पर्सनैलिटी को ज्यादा आकर्षक बना देती है? क्या आक्रामक ड्राइविंग को महिलाएं आत्मविश्वास समझती हैं या असुरक्षा की निशानी? क्या सड़क पर दबंगई दिखाना प्रभाव छोड़ता है या नकारात्मक छवि बनाता है? और सबसे अहम, क्या थार की लोकप्रिय छवि पुरुषों की कल्पना है या महिलाओं की भी यही राय है? इस वीडियो में हम इन्हीं सवालो का जवाब जानने की कोशिश कर रहे हैं. पल्टीमार नेताओं पर जनता ने क्या कहा? राम मंदिर में चंदा चोरी: किसे जिम्मेदार मानती है जनता?

items.title: Masculinity or negative aura farming: What do people really think of Thar drivers?
items.summary: Scroll through Instagram or YouTube and you’ll find many videos of loud exhausts, reckless driving, traffic-rule speedruns, and a whole lot of attitude. Somewhere along the way, the Mahindra Thar has become less about off-roading and more about making an entrance for many. Does a big SUV scream confidence, or insecurity? Is road aggression impressive, or just cringe? And is the Thar’s “alpha male” image something women buy into or something men have convinced themselves of? We hit the streets to ask people one simple question: What’s your first impression of a guy in a Thar? The answers weren’t what many Thar owners would expect. Small teams can do great things. All it takes is a subscription. Subscribe now and power Newslaundry’s work.

items.title: ‘Feels like career over’: The online campaign to intimidate women part of CJP protest
items.summary: A BJP MLA posts a video of a bleeding, weeping girl and tells his followers she is being taught a lesson. The video is actually from Varanasi, from a domestic violence case, and has nothing to do with the protest. It does not matter. The comments say: she didn’t get beaten enough . In the two weeks since the Cockroach Janata Party’s July 20 Parliament march, more than half a dozen women and girls who appeared in clips from CJP protests have been identified across X, Instagram and Facebook – by an elected legislator, by Hindutva handles with large followings, by strangers who have sought to file police complaints and published home addresses. They face threats of rape and death. There are other consequences too. A yoga instructor has lost many of her clients, a widowed mother has lost her tuition work, a teenager’s family home stands locked. The case that has drawn the most television attention is that of Ruchika Singh, a 15-year-old filmed at Jantar Mantar using expletives against Prime Minister Modi, who now faces charges of defamation and “intentional insult to provoke breach of peace”. Late on Friday night, Modi posted a video saying he had been subjected to all kinds of abuse during the protests, and that he forgave everyone. She posted her own soon after – she had fallen under the influence of certain YouTubers that day, she said; she was ashamed; she apologised to him and to the country. It did not end. Users began matching stills from the apology against footage from the protest – eyebrows, nose piercings, hair colour, teeth – to argue that the two were different girls. An account named Khetan Anup posted several such videos. “The two girls don’t look alike,” one caption read. “Something seems fishy here.” The case against Ruchika Ravi Negi, the BJP MLA from East Delhi's Patparganj constituency, known locally for turning up in Mayur Vihar to demand shopkeepers’ names, shared the Varanasi video on his social media account days after the march. He then shared a second video , filmed inside his own office, showing two or three men seated around him working out a girl’s address. She is a resident of Mandawali, in East Delhi, they establish. “First, we will have her summoned to the police station,” Negi says. In another video , he says: “We will definitely find the girl today or tomorrow. She will have to apologise in a public place. We will take legal action against her.” The girl from Mandawali had raised questions about the gates of the Hanuman Temple

items.title: Masking number plate of vehicle a violation under MV Act but not cheating under IPC: Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently quashed a cheating case against a man who was booked for riding a scooter with its rear number plate covered by a black mask [ Mohammed Abdul Ahad Shaker v. State of Telangana ]. In an order passed on July 28, a Bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih held that merely obstructing a vehicle's number plate would not constitute the offence of cheating under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC) unless the essential ingredients of the offence are established. The Court clarified that covering the number plate of a vehicle could amount to a regulatory violation under the Motor Vehicles Act (MV Act) but such a violation could not be converted into a cheating offence. “ The regulatory breach of obstructing the number plate under the MV Act and rules thereunder cannot be dressed as an offence under Section 420 of the IPC without establishing the essential ingredients as required, ” the Court said. Justice Sanjay Karol & Justice Augustine George Masih The Court was hearing an appeal filed by Mohammed Abdul Ahad Shaker against the Telangana High Court's refusal to quash the criminal proceedings against him. The case arose in June 2020, when Shaker was stopped by a police officer while riding a black Honda Activa in Hyderabad with a black mask covering its rear number plate. An FIR was subsequently registered against him under Section 420 IPC and Section 80(a) of the Motor Vehicles Act. The police alleged that he had covered the number plate to deceive them and avoid traffic challans. A chargesheet was filed in August 2020, following which a magistrate took cognisance of the case. In September 2025, Shaker approached the Telangana High Court seeking to quash the proceedings. The High Court rejected his plea, holding that a prima facie case was made out and observing that the number plate could not have been masked under any circumstances. This led to the appeal before the Supreme Court. Before the Supreme Court, Shaker's counsel argued that merely covering the rear number plate did not satisfy the ingredients of cheating under Section 420 IPC. It was also argued that if Shaker had actually intended to evade identification, he would have covered the front number plate as well. The State opposed the appeal and maintained that a prima facie case had been made out. The Supreme Court agreed with Shaker's contention. items.title: Punjab spending large amount of money on freebies, ads but not paying dues to employees: P&H High Court
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Monday observed that the Punjab government was spending huge amounts of money on freebies and advertisements but withholding legitimate dues of its own employees citing financial constraints. A Division Bench of Acting Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor made the observation in a judgment directing Punjab government to release up-to-date pending installments of dearness allowance/ dearness relief (DA/DR) to all its employees and pensioners. The Court also said that Punjab shall not resort to any unproductive expenditures such as large-scale advertising campaigns in print or social media, till these dues are cleared. "While the issue of financial constraints is being raised as a ground for withholding the legitimate dues of the State’s own employees, however, as per the information available in the public domain, the State is expending large amounts of money on grant of freebies, doles, advertorial campaigns, and other expenditure, which would not strictly fall within the domain of essential expenditure by a welfare State, cannot be brushed aside, lightly," the Court said. Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor The Court ruled that the legitimate dues payable to the employees of the State cannot be withheld on the ground of any new alleged welfare schemes. "Viewed in any manner, large scale advertising campaigns in print or social media and other unproductive expenses cannot justify denial of dues admissible to the State employees," the Bench added. The Court was dealing with petitions rejecting Punjab government and Punjab State Power Corporation Limited (PSPCL)'s appeals challenging a single-judge verdict. The single-judge had on April 8 directed the State and PSPCL to release till June 30 all up-to-date pending installments of DA or DR to all its employees and pensioners at the same rates as has been paid to the members of the All India Services (IAS/IPS/IFS) serving within Punjab. In 2021, Punjab government had approved the recommendation of the 6th Pay Commission to grant DA/DR to the State employees on the Central government pattern. However, despite the approval, it failed to release the amounts. This led to multiple petitions before the High Court. items.title: Consumer court asks dry cleaner to compensate man for burning wedding sherwani
items.summary: A Chhattisgarh consumer court recently asked a dry cleaner to compensate a customer whose wedding sherwani was burnt during pressing [ Dageshwar Yadav v. Ashok Nirmalkar ]. In an order passed on July 1, the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission at Raipur held that damaging a customer’s garment while providing dry cleaning services amounts to deficiency in service and unfair trade practice under consumer law. “By the opposite party ruining the sherwani of the complainant by burning while pressing and not paying its price to the complainant… deficiency in service and unfair trade practice has been done by him,” the Commission held. The case goes back to September 2019, when the customer, one Dageshwar Yadav, dropped off four pieces of wedding attire, including a sherwani worth around ₹12,000, at a dry cleaning shop in Chandrakhuri village. When he got his clothes back, the area near the sherwani’s second button had been burnt through, apparently by the hot press. Yadav says he asked the shop owner, Ashok Nirmalkar, to pay for the damage several times, but was met only with excuses, and eventually, an outright refusal. He first tried the police, filing a written complaint the same day the damage was discovered. The police, however, treated it as a non-cognizable matter and told him to approach the courts instead. Yadav filed his consumer complaint in November 2019, nearly seven years before the case was finally argued in June 2026. Throughout the proceedings, Nirmalkar never showed up. Despite being served notice, he filed no written response, no affidavit, and no documents disputing Yadav’s version of events. The Commission noted that this left Yadav’s evidence - a police complaint, photographs of the burnt sherwani, a legal notice, and a bill for the garment - entirely unchallenged. However, the Commission didn’t accept Yadav’s compensation claim in full. It noted that the bill he submitted for the sherwani was produced nearly seven years after the incident, with no explanation for the delay, and did not appear to be reliable. Instead of the claimed ₹12,000, the Commission estimated the sherwani’s value at ₹6,000. It also trimmed down Yadav’s demand of ₹5,000 for physical, financial and mental distress to ₹3,000, finding the original figure excessive. It accordingly directed Nirmalkar to pay Yadav ₹6,000 for the sherwani, with 6% annual interest calculated from the date the complaint was filed in 2019, along with ₹3,000 as compensation and ₹5,000

items.title: We don't want any dog to die: Delhi HC directs MCD, NDMC to hold camps for sterilisation/vaccination of stray dogs
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Monday directed the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) and New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) to hold a camp in every ward in the national capital for vaccination and sterilisation of stray dogs. The Bench of Justice Dinesh Mehta and Justice Rajneesh Kumar Gupta passed the order in a suo motu public interest litigation (PIL) case on the issue of stray dog management of stray dogs. "MCD and NDMC shall organise a camp, one ward each in its respective area for installation of the stray dogs. This shall be taken as a pilot project. Prior publicity of the camp in its areas shall be done. Placard shall be displayed with wide publicity that the stray dogs are not being captured or being sent to dog pounds and they are being brought to camp only for the purpose of vaccination/sterilisation," the Court directed. It suggested the MCD to start with areas with areas frequented by people. "Let us go by small area, smaller part, select ward like, near Connaught Place, India Gate. More offices are there. Let us go by that in this ward, all dogs are sterilised," the Bench said. Justice Dinesh Mehta and Justice Rajneesh Kumar Gupta Meanwhile, one of the judges on the bench said his mother was bitten twice by dogs. "We are taking care of dog biting. Yes, they are a threat to everyone. Dog has bitten my mother twice. It is a harsh reality. Dogs do bite. Bhagwan Kare kisi ko nahi kaate. Let us not go into this, it is a problem. Everyday you will find dogs biting. I don't want to get into this, kutta kaat ta hai ki nahi kaat ta," Justice Mehta said. The Court, however, remarked that while it does not want dog bite incidents to occur anywhere, it wants a percentage of dogs to remain for future generations. "We don't want any dog to die, even they [government] don't want any dog to die...This is not adversarial. From today onwards, we don't want to hear, dog kaat gaya, dog nahi kaata, sabko pata hai kaat-ta hai. I will cry when dogs go, I still say 5 percent population should be left so that the next generation sees the dog," the Bench said. In response to concerns expressed by a dog feeder, the Court said, "There are millions of dogs. In all colonies, will allow a person to take their dogs. We just want to hold a camp, one responsible person who can make a list of the dogs." items.title: Madras High Court refuses to restrain release of AI-enhanced version of Rajinikanth’s Kochadaiiyaan
items.summary: The Madras High Court on July 31 refused to restrain the release of an Artificial Intelligence-enhanced or remastered version of the Rajinikanth-starrer film Kochadaiiyaan [ Ad Bureau Advertising Vs MediaOne ] Justice K Kumaresh Babu dismissed an interim application filed as part of a long running financial dispute between Ad Bureau Advertising Private Limited and the film's producer, Mediaone Global Entertainment Ltd. Ad Bureau Advertising is reported to have lent money to the producer of Kochadaiiyaan to provide financing for the film's post-production. In 2015, the ad agency filed a money recovery suit against Mediaone Global Entertainment and others connected to the film such as Mediaone Global's director Dr J Murali Manohar, the film's promoter Latha Rajinikanth, and the film's director Soundarya Rajinikanth. This year, it was announced that a remastered version of the film would be released by production house Eros International Media Limited. This led Ad Bureau Advertising to file an interim application before the High Court to restrain any such re-release of the film while its money recovery suit remains pending. The Court, on July 31, dismissed this application after noting that Eros admittedly now held rights to the film. "The plaintiff had not sought for any relief as against the fifth defendant (Eros), who is admittedly now assignee of the film. When that being so, the claim of the applicant to prevent the re-release of the film... could not be entertained by this Court at the present stage," it said. Justice K Kumaresh Babu The money recovery suit arose from agreements executed in April and May 2014 and a deed of guarantee dated May 4, 2014. Ad Bureau claimed it transferred ₹10 crore to finance the film and that the defendants had agreed to repay ₹20.40 crore, along with granting collection rights in Tamil Nadu. However, these repayment obligations were allegedly not honoured, prompting Ad Bureau to file its money recovery suit, apart from filing a cheque dishonour case. In its latest application, the ad agency argued that the re-release of the film could affect its claims in the money recovery suit. Appearing in person, Ad Bureau Managing Director Abirchand Nahar told the Court that the defendants had allegedly failed to honour cheques and an undertaking given by them before the Supreme Court in related proceedings. items.title: P&H High Court bars Punjab government from large-scale advertising till payment of DA to employees, pensioners
items.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court on Monday barred Punjab government from issuing any large-scale advertising campaigns till it releases Dearness Allowance (DA) to employees and pensioners in compliance with a recent judgment of a single-bench. A Bench of Acting Chief Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor passed the direction while rejecting Punjab government and Punjab State Power Corporation Limited (PSPCL)'s appeals challenging a single-judge verdict. The single-judge had on April 8 directed the State and PSPCL to release till June 30 all up-to-date pending installments of DA or Dearness Relief (DR) to all its employees and pensioners at the same rates as has been paid to the members of the All India Services (IAS/IPS/IFS) serving within Punjab. Today, the Division Bench said the payment be done within a fortnight and in case of default, the unpaid amounts shall carry simple interest of 6 percent per annum. The Court said a compliance report be filed before end of this month. "Till all such dues are cleared, the State of Punjab shall not resort to any unproductive expenditures such as large-scale advertising campaigns in print or social media as these expenses cannot justify the denial of dues admissible to State employees," the Bench ordered. Justice Ashwani Kumar Mishra and Justice Rohit Kapoor In 2021, Punjab government had approved the recommendation of the 6th Pay Commission to grant DA/DR to the State employees on the Central Government pattern. However, despite the approval, it failed to release the amounts. Consequently, a number of petition were filed to seek release of the dues. The Court was told employees and pensioners of the State were being paid 16% less DA than All India Service Officers. In response, Punjab government cited financial constraints. It also referred to a liquidation plan under which the payment of pension was staggered based on the age of pensioners. The same had also been adopted by the PSPCL for its pensioners. In April, Justice Harpreet Singh Brar ruled that this plan was violative of Article 14 as it created an impermissible differentiation within a homogeneous class of pensioners. The judge then directed the PSPCL to release the arrears of revised pension/family pension (including DR arrears) as per 6th Punjab Pay Commission to all their pensioners and family pensioners. The State government and PSPCL challenged the judgment. Today, the appeals were dismissed. Advocate General Maninderjit Singh Bedi ,
